first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this, so I'll read the lot. The intro is calm and plain, no silly slang. I liked that it says it will cover marrying legally in Brazil and travelling there safely. That's the part I actually care about, the customs are lovely but I'm the one asking about the paperwork.

journey.quote: It says plainly which meanings are documented and which are simply often told.
journey.reaction: Good. I don't like being sold fairy tales. Someone being honest about what's folklore makes me trust the rest.

journey.quote: Treat everything below as a menu to discuss with both families, not a checklist that every wedding follows.
journey.reaction: Sensible. Two families, two sets of expectations. That's exactly the conversation we'll be having around the kitchen table.

journey.section: Noivado and the ring on the right hand
journey.quote: Many Brazilian families expect an engagement celebration of some kind, so it is worth asking early whether one is planned, especially if relatives will travel for both.
journey.reaction: Two lots of travel for the older relatives. That's a cost and a strain I hadn't thought of. Useful.

journey.quote: UNESCO describes it as music, dance and poetry that developed in the Recôncavo region of Bahia from the seventeenth century, drawing on the traditions of the region's enslaved Africans and on Portuguese elements.
journey.reaction: Interesting enough, but it's three long paragraphs about UNESCO lists. I skimmed this bit. It's not what I'll be forwarding to my husband.

journey.quote: When you choose a venue, ask for its music curfew, last finish time and late-food options in writing.
journey.reaction: In writing. Yes. That's how I like things done.

journey.quote: This section reflects official sources as at November 2026. It is general information, not legal advice, and requirements can change.
journey.reaction: Dated and honest about its limits. I appreciate that, but it also tells me the legal side is ours to sort out.

journey.quote: Whether the cartório also needs a sworn Portuguese translation of your documents, and which ones, is a question to put to the cartório and the Embassy, including any fees.
journey.reaction: This is my worry exactly: documents and contracts in Portuguese. The article keeps saying 'ask the cartório'. Who asks them? My daughter doesn't speak Portuguese well and I certainly don't. Nobody here says they'll help with that.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for venue, travel and suppliers, with the fee and inclusions agreed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking. One person, fee in writing before anything is paid. That's what I want to hear. I'd still want to know their name and speak to them on the phone.

journey.quote: The legal steps above stay with you, the cartório and the Embassy.
journey.reaction: Fair enough to be upfront, but it leaves me wondering who chases the paperwork in a foreign language. Is there at least a translator or local contact they can put us onto?

journey.quote: As at 3 November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise a high degree of caution" in Brazil overall because of the threat of violent crime, with no higher-level areas.
journey.reaction: I'm glad they didn't hide this. I'd have looked it up anyway. It does make me more nervous about my mother travelling.

journey.quote: Travel insurance should cover medical costs, including evacuation.
journey.reaction: Good, practical. But there's nothing about older guests at all: long flights, wheelchairs, hospitals near the venue. My mother is 88.

journey.quote: Drink spiking and methanol poisoning occur, so serve only branded, sealed drinks.
journey.reaction: Alarming, but I'd rather know. I'll be telling the bar staff myself.

journey.section: Planning a Brazilian wedding, wherever it happens
journey.quote: When you are ready to plan, a Wedded Advisor can be your single point of contact from the first conversation, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Repeated, and I'm glad. Still nothing on deposits to Brazilian suppliers, or who I ring if something goes wrong on the day.

unanswered_questions: Is the deposit protected if a Brazilian supplier or venue goes under or disappears?
Are supplier contracts in Portuguese and in reais, and does someone check them or translate them for us?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Brazilian time? Is there anyone on the ground during the wedding?
Can the Wedded Advisor help with older guests: accessible transfers, step-free venues, hospitals nearby?
Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor on the phone before anything is booked, and will I know their name?
Can the Advisor put us onto a sworn translator or someone who deals with the cartório, even if the legal steps are ours?

turn_offs_found.quote: The [Samba de Roda of the Recôncavo of Bahia] was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2008.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a turn-off as such, but the UNESCO section is long and reads like an encyclopaedia. On the iPad it's a wall of text I scrolled past.

would_share_with: My husband, with the legal and Smartraveller sections marked and my questions about deposits and Mum's mobility
My daughter, to ask which customs her fiancé's family will expect

cta_reaction.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for venue, travel and suppliers, with the fee and inclusions agreed in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: Fee in writing and one point of contact is exactly right. I'd click if it said I could book a phone call and that they'd help with older relatives and protect our deposits. As it stands I'd probably let my daughter click and ask her to put me on the call.

top_3_changes: Add a sentence on older or less mobile guests in the Brazil travel section (accessible transfers, step-free venues, medical access) and say the Advisor can plan around it.
Say what happens with deposits and supplier contracts in Portuguese and reais: who checks them and how payments are protected.
Make the Wedded Advisor offer concrete: a phone call before anything is booked, a named person, and who to contact on the day if something goes wrong.

checks.note: All journey items, turn-offs and CTA reaction quote the draft text exactly.

[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments treated as invisible.

Can one line on elderly or mobility-limited guests be added to the Brazil travel notes from Smartraveller or another sourced page, without inventing Advisor services?
